facts.text: MullerBrownDiscrete-v0 is registered with env_kwargs m=5 and n=5, so the environment opens on a 5 by 5 grid by default
m and n are the number of grid points along the x and y axes
The grid extent is x from -1.5 to 1 and y from -0.5 to 2
The x and y grid coordinates are linspace over that extent with m and n points
The observation space is MultiDiscrete([m, n]) and the action space is Discrete(5)
Actions 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 are up one grid point (+y), down (-y), left (-x), right (+x) and do nothing
Each term is A[k] * exp(a[k]*(x-x0[k])**2 + b[k]*(x-x0[k])*(y-y0[k]) + c[k]*(y-y0[k])**2), summed over the four terms
An on-grid step rewards old_energy - new_energy, the decrease in potential energy
An off-grid move is penalized by a reward of -100 and leaves the agent at its current position
step always returns done=False: the environment has no pre-set endpoint
reset() draws the starting state from observation_space.sample()
The README describes a discretized 2-D Muller-Brown potential in a gym-compatible format, a GridWorld variant with no pre-set endpoint
The README defines the potential over X = [-1.5, 1.0] and Y = [-0.5, 2.0]

determinism.notes: the fake's reset(seed=...) seeds the observation space's Python RNG and the step rule is deterministic, so a fresh world repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the upstream reset() takes no seed and samples an unseeded observation_space (the imported gym.utils.seeding is unused), so seeded repeatability is a property of the fake, not of the upstream class, and a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two

gaps: kinematic/analytic grid world: the agent moves between the m by n grid points of an analytic Muller-Brown potential; there are no continuous dynamics, no forces, no contacts and no actuator, sensor or noise model, and timestep_ms is 0 because one tick is one grid move with no physical duration
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0; only commands advance the world and ticks do not model elapsed time

the fake draws the start state with a seeded Python random.Random and evaluates the energy with math.exp, while the upstream class samples numpy's observation space (unseeded) and uses numpy float arithmetic, so a seed does not repeat the same trajectory on the two and numbers can differ in the last bits

render/plotPES and matplotlib are not modelled and cap.world.render.v1 is unbound; snapshot/restore are not offered because the upstream class has no get_state()/set_state() pair (its set_state() only sets the agent position)
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the grid state is kept and stays readable
